MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  September 4, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Tuesday,
September 4, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Public Works Director
Damasse, City Attorney Hogin, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3. PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Gazeley read a proclamation recognizing and honoring Parks and Recreation Director
Cindy Blount for her thirty six years of service to the City of Lomita.

Mayor Gazeley announced that the Certificate of Appointment to the Public Safety and Traffic
Commission would be mailed to new Commissioner Mauro Dominguez, since he was not in
attendance.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed the public that the pedestrian crosswalk at Narbonne Avenue and
243rd Street had been repaired and was now fully operational, while the second pedestrian
crosswalk at Narbonne and 245th Street had been referred to the Public Safety and Traffic
Commission for review.

  Page 1 of 8
 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested that the following new items to be placed on a future agenda:

  1. Consideration of placing recycling containers in all City parks. Councilmember Sanchez
  seconded this agenda item request. The motion to place the item on a future agenda
  carried unanimously.

  2. Consideration of a Dog Park in Lomita. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the agenda
  item request. The motion to place the item on a future agenda carried as follows:

  Ayes: Councilmembers Traina, Sanchez, and Savidan
  Noes: Councilmember Estrada and Mayor Gazeley

Councilmember Traina asked for the status of scheduling these items on a future agenda:

  3. Discussion regarding the citywide flooding issues. City Manager Rock stated that this
  item will be brought before City Council for discussion on either September 17, 2012, or
  October 1, 2012.

  4. Discussion regarding having a balanced budget for the next fiscal year. City Manager
  Rock informed City Council that he is currently working on scheduling a goal-setting
  retreat with Council in late January or early February 2013, during which balancing the
  budget for Fiscal Year 2013-2014 would be discussed.

  5. Presentation by WaterWorks to the City Council. City Manager Rock stated that this
  request is currently in conflict with a closed session issues, and since there is potential
  litigation regarding the reservoir, it is not advisable to have such a presentation from
  WaterWorks.

Councilmember Traina asked staff to look into the following item:

Whether there is adequate painting of red curb at 241st Street, near the intersection of
Narbonne and Pennsylvania.

Mayor Gazeley informed everyone that a retirement party for Cindy Blount is currently
scheduled for 11 a.m., on September 22, 2012, at Lomita Park. Mayor Gazeley also announced
that the annual 9/11 event is scheduled for 6:30 p.m., on September 11, 2012, in front of City
Hall.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked if the City is meeting its goals for recyclables. According
to Mr. McGrath, some people pick-up recyclables at the curb of his house before the scheduled
trash pick-up. Mr. McGrath also expressed his concern over the safety involving low-flying
airplanes over Lomita. Lastly, Mr. McGrath wanted to know if there would be some kind of
enforcement on September 17, 2012, if the “No Texting While Driving” proclamation is approved.

  Page 2 of 8
 In response to Mr. McGrath, Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the City has had no
issues in the past meeting minimum recyclable rates, and that the City’s Code Enforcement
would follow-up on the scavenging issues in Mr. McGrath’s neighborhood. Also responding to
Mr. McGrath, City Manager Rock stated that there will be enforcement on September 17, 2012,
regarding “No Texting While Driving.”

Ernie Moore, Lomita resident, informed the City Council that his previously submitted claim for
construction related damages on Avocado Street had been forwarded to the Claims
Management Company in Orange County, and to date no contact has been made by the
investigator. Mr. Moore stated that he will be escalating the claim to the next level on
September 14, 2012.

Marty Spain, Lomita resident, congratulated Cindy Blount on her retirement. Mr. Spain also
requested fiscal accountability from the City, and asked that water services be contracted out.

James Thompson, First Vice President of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked
Councilmembers Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley for attending the most recent business
mixer at Harry’s Smokehouse BBQ. Mr. Thompson also announced that the next business
mixer is scheduled for September 27, 2012, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., at the Lomita Railroad
Museum.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that he was pleased to see that the crosswalk at
Narbonne Avenue has been fixed, but added that it should have been fixed before someone got
hurt. Mr. Kivett also asked that the City Council consider keeping and repairing the second
crosswalk, since people are used to it and would continue crossing at that location even if the
crosswalk was removed.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, noted that a Dog Park is needed in Lomita. Mr. Friedrich also
talked about the importance of transparency in government, and stated that residents want to be
kept informed regarding issues and improvements or development going on in Lomita.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, informed City Council that according to a printout he obtained from
the California Water Service Company website, only 10% of the company's revenue goes
toward payroll expenditures, while the remainders of revenues are spent on capital
improvements projects, conservation, etc.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Traina
requested that Item 6.I. be pulled from the Consent Agenda for discussion. Councilmember
Sanchez seconded the motion to approve the Consent Agenda, minus Item 6.I, which carried
unanimously.

Councilmember Traina indicated that half of the contract amount for Item 6.I, “Actuarial
Services,” is budgeted under the General Fund, while the other half is budgeted under the Water
Enterprise Fund. Councilmember Traina further pointed out that the allocation for “Actuarial
Services” is much higher than the salary allocation to the Water Enterprise Fund, which he
stated was around 33%. Administrative Services Director Chavez responded that staff used the
same methodology for “Actuarial Services” as was used for the City’s Audit Services, which is
  Page 3 of 8
 an equal distribution between the General Fund and the Water Enterprise Fund. Discussion
followed on whether the cost budgeted under the Water Enterprise Fund was reasonable, and if
the percentage allocated to the Water Enterprise Fund could be lowered.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve Item 6.I. Councilmember Estrada seconded the
motion. The motion carried as follows:

Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
Noes: Councilmember Traina

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on August 20,
  2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Report dealing with economic development activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Report dealing with activities of the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND
  FILE.

  f. Report dealing with activities of the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Report presenting the Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Proclamation declaring September 19, 2012, as “It Can Wait – No Texting While Driving
  Pledge Day.”

  i.  Award of Professional Services Agreement for Actuarial Valuation Study with Howard E.
  Nyhart Company, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $6,000. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

8. CYPRESS  WATER  PRODUCTION  FACILITY  (CWPF)  OFFLINE  TESTING
  RECOMMENDATIONS

Public Works Director Damasse provided an overview of the agenda report. According to
Director Damasse, currently Well No. 5 at the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF) has
been voluntarily shut down due to various water quality issues, which are primarily aesthetic and
cosmetic secondary issues associated with iron, manganese, hardness, total dissolved solids,
odor, and taste; Director Damasse emphasized that no tests have been conducted since 2010.
Director Damasse stated that the Kennedy and Jenks feasibility analysis report was presented
to City Council in March of 2012, which outlined potential solutions to address various water
quality concerns. On June 18, 2012, the City Council formed the CWPF Water Subcommittee.
According to Director Damasse, the purpose of the CWPF Water Subcommittee was to review
and analyze data relative to water quality, consult with other water agencies, and formulate
recommendations regarding the future operation of the CWPF. Therefore, Director Damasse

  Page 4 of 8
 stated that based on direction provided at the CWPF Water Subcommittee meetings, staff and
the CWPF Water Subcommittee are recommending the following:

  •  Establish the treatment objectives/goals for water distribution through the CWPF;
  •  Conduct temporary offline testing at the CWPF, without distributing the water to
  customers; and
  •  Authorize staff to solicit proposals in order to retain an independent consulting firm to
  oversee the testing and implementation of a public relations campaign for the project.

Councilmember Traina emphasized that the main goal is to have the highest quality water,
regardless whether it is primary or secondary quality issues, as indicated in the staff report.
Furthermore, Councilmember Traina questioned the budgeted expense for public relations
outreach, and asked why the public relations portion of the project could not be performed in-
house. Director Damasse responded that the cost for public relations outreach will be minimal
since the component of the project would be a collaborative effort between City staff and the
West Basin Municipal Water District; Director Damasse stated that West Basin will be providing
the technical analysis for the public relations outreach.

Councilmember Traina expressed his concerns with the proposed water quality testing ranges,
and suggested establishing lower ranges so the best quality water is provided to Lomita
residents. Councilmember Traina also inquired as to what was proposed differently this time, in
comparison with what was proposed a couple months earlier, when the water blending request
was postponed by City Council. Director Damasse responded that this time other options, such
as residual management system treatment and chemical injections acid addition, are not
mentioned. Director Damasse added that the improvements completed at the reservoir facility
since 2010 mostly hydraulic in nature would help significantly with the blending process. The
improvements made include the following: inlet piping installation, the downstream
improvements to PCH and the use of the booster pump station at Appian Way.

Discussion followed on whether the water quality would change in comparison with that of 2010.
In support of testing, City Manager Rock stated that significant changes had been made to the
Water Treatment Plant since 2010. The City installed a Solar Bee Mixer in August 2010 and
installed temporary blending pipes in late 2010 after Well No. 5 was shut down. These and
other changes may change the quality of the water as compared to what residents received in
August 2010.

Councilmember Traina asked if staff could provide a reasonable breakdown of all of the costs
involved in the operations of the Water Treatment Plant, including staffing and operational
expenses, as he would like to see if it would be viable and more cost efficient for the City to
operate the Water Treatment Plant on its own, rather than simply purchasing water from
Metropolitan. Councilmember Traina also inquired as to what would be the proposed ratio of
blended water in order to make the blending process economically profitable for the City. City
Manager Rock responded that water purchases from Metropolitan should be 50% or less.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that the City Council wants the best quality water for residents,
and that water testing is required to find out what could be done to fix current water quality
issues. Councilmember Sanchez went on to reassure residents that the water provided to
customers would be high quality water.

  Page 5 of 8
 In response to Councilmember Traina’s question regarding savings due to cheaper well water
production, and what would happen with the savings, City Manager Rock stated that savings
accumulated from cheaper well water production would stabilize water rates and provide an
increase to the capital improvement fund, which in turn could be used to replace water lines that
have been in place since the 1920s. Councilmember Sanchez added that water rates could be
revisited once Council makes a final decision regarding the reservoir.

Councilmember Savidan reiterated that the goal is to provide the highest quality water to
constituents.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita Resident, stated that he was concerned with the chemicals that would be
used to treat water and the possible health effects to residents. Mr. Friedrich also stated that
proposed ranges for water hardness seemed very high, and he suggested lowering the ranges
for water hardness, as indicated in the staff report, or at least to match the Metropolitan average
water hardness rate.

Rob Katherman, Water Replenishment District Director, stated that the total cost of ground water
would be $400-410 per acre foot, which includes a $244 per acre foot water replenishment
assessment and about $150-160 per acre foot for operations and maintenance costs, as
compared to Metropolitan water, which costs a little over $1,000 per acre foot. Mr. Katherman
added that historically ground water operations and maintenance costs increase 3-4% per year,
while imported water increases at an average rate of 8% per year. Furthermore, Mr. Katherman
noted that it is wise for municipalities to have control over their own water supply, instead of
relying on imported water, as several factors could significantly reduce delivery of imported
water from the Delta, including earthquakes, biological issues, and regulatory issues.

Richard Nagel, General Manager of West Basin Municipal Water District (WBMWD), stated that
WBMWD is the regional provider of water for the South Bay, and currently serves 17 cities in the
area. According to Mr. Nagel, 60% of water provided to constituents is imported, while 40% is
ground water, and that WBMWD is trying to reduce its dependence on outside water, from 60%
to 30%. Mr. Nagel added that blending water is a very common practice, and in many cases is
a best management practice; Mr. Nagel recommended developing locally-controlled projects
related to water supply.

Councilmember Sanchez asked Mr. Nagel if Metropolitan was planning to have significant
increases in water rates over the next several years. Mr. Nagel responded that due to
significant increases in capital improvement project rates in the last four to five years, water
rates will be increasing in the future.

In response to Mayor Gazeley’s question regarding potential future water supply problems, Mr.
Nagel responded that climate conditions, such as droughts, or disasters, like earthquakes, could
be devastating for water supplies, therefore, Mr. Nagel emphasized that local control over water
supply is imperative.

Discussion followed whether the cost of testing and water analysis could be lower than the
proposed budget of $80,000.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked City Council to test the well water first, in order to find out
what is wrong with the water before the blending process occurs. Mr. McGrath also questioned
  Page 6 of 8
 the cost of testing and getting the well operational, as well as what the costs would be to
residents.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, was concerned with contamination in the water, and reiterated
that the City should test the well water first, in order to find out the cause of the problem.

Patty Boge, Lomita resident, asked if the $80,000 requested for water testing was a budgeted
expense, and if it was, then why was it being brought for discussion. City Manager Rock
responded that the requested amount of $80,000 was a budgeted expense under the Water
Enterprise Fund, however, since the Water Treatment Plant is not operational, and in an effort to
eliminate any public misconceptions and allegations of not being transparent, staff decided to
present this item for Council discussion. Ms. Boge also asked what would happen if the results
of the testing end up being not to standard. City Manager Rock responded that the testing
results would be presented to City Council, and that City Council would then have to decide on
whether to continue purchasing water from Metropolitan, or look into other treatment options.

Clay Gorbet, Lomita resident, questioned the reliability of the data, since water testing has not
been done since 2010.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, asked why staff believes that the results of blending would be any
different from the 2010 test results, as not that many changes have been made to the actual
water treatment process. Mr. Albert also asked City Council to set lower ranges for water
hardness, and recommended that a third party conduct the testing. Furthermore, Mr. Albert
asked if staff had included in the budget the cost of purchasing Metropolitan water for blending.
Lastly, Mr. Albert wanted to know what chemicals would be used for testing. Director Damasse
responded to Mr. Albert’s questions regarding the use of chemicals and improvements made to
the Water Treatment Plant since 2010.

City Manager Rock stated that the residents need to know that the water from Well No.5 is not
contaminated; it is potable and drinkable, and it is not pond water.

Mayor Gazeley thanked all the speakers.

Councilmember Traina reiterated that the City Council's goal is to provide quality water for all
citizens, which is the most important thing to do.

Councilmember Sanchez stated that the primary issue is to test the well water, and then blend
the water at different ratios, and test the various blends.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to accept the recommendations of staff and to start the
blending process at the Cypress Water Production Facility. Councilmember Savidan seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Sanchez added that the City Council wanted an independent, outside
consultant to perform the water blending and testing.

Regular City Council meeting was adjourned at 9:35 p.m., to go to closed session.

  Page 7 of 8
   CLOSED SESSION

9. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – Existing Litigation

 Pursuant to Government Code section 54956.9(a)
 Islamic Center of the South Bay v. City of Lomita, et al.
 United States District Court LA CV12-02418

10. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – Anticipated Litigation

 Pursuant to Government Code section 54956.9(b)
 Number of Potential Cases: 1
 Letter from Steven H. Rosenbaum, to City Attorney, dated July 24, 2012

11. ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

The City Council reconvened at 10:22 p.m. City Attorney Hogin announced that the City Council
had met in closed session, discussed the items on the closed session agenda but had not taken
any reportable action.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 10:23 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
